title: Open localization and affine realization of supplied dualizing pairs and their morphisms
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes with $S$ locally Noetherian [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Put $Y=X\times_SX$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with first projection $p_1$ and closed diagonal $\Delta$. Let $(K,\xi)$ and $(L,\eta)$ be supplied coherent relative dualizing pairs [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]: $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category] are pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] and locally have finite Tor amplitude over $S$ [def-pc-finite-tor-dimension-over], and the classes from $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X$ to $Lp_1^*K,Lp_1^*L$ induce the multiplication isomorphisms to the corresponding derived internal Hom [def-pc-derived-pullback], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For every open $j:W\hookrightarrow X$, including the empty open, $f|_W$ is again separated, flat and locally finitely presented, and $(K|_W,\xi|_{W\times_SW})$ and $(L|_W,\eta|_{W\times_SW})$ are supplied pairs for $W/S$. In particular $(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X)|_{W\times_SW}=\Delta_{W*}\mathcal O_W$, and the derived pullback, class multiplication and scalar maps restrict to those for $W/S$. Now take affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ with $f(U)\subset V$ and $R$ Noetherian, and put $B=A\otimes_RA$. For $T=K,L$ set $M_T=R\Gamma(U,T|_U)\in D(A)$, using the affine derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence]. The affine diagonal-class comparison [lem-trf-affine-relative-dualizing-comparison] gives pseudo-coherent $M_T$ of finite $R$-Tor amplitude and the actual classes $\gamma_K,\gamma_L:A\to M_T\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B$. There are natural isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal O_U)$
$$\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_K,M_T)}\cong R\mathcal Hom_U(K|_U,T|_U),$$
where tilde is termwise associated sheaf. For $T=K$ this identifies the algebraic scalar map with the restriction of $\mathcal O_X\to R\mathcal Hom_X(K,K)$. For every integer $i$ it induces $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(M_K,M_T[i])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_U)}(K|_U,T|_U[i])$. Isomorphisms $a:M_K\to M_L$ correspond bijectively to isomorphisms $\alpha_U:K|_U\to L|_U$, and $(a\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,p_1}B)\gamma_K=\gamma_L$ if and only if $(Lp_{1,U}^*\alpha_U)\xi_U=\eta_U$. These identifications respect scalar multiplication, composition and further open restrictions wherever the charts are defined.

proof.text: Write $Y_W=W\times_S W\subset Y$. The inverse image of this open under $\Delta$ is $W$, and the restricted closed subscheme is exactly the diagonal of $W/S$ (restrict its defining ideal). Thus $f|_W$ is separated. Its stalk maps are the stalk maps of $f$, so it is flat. For local finite presentation choose, around any $w\in W$, an affine neighbourhood $U\subset W$ mapping into an affine $V\subset S$; [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] applies directly to these affine opens of $X,S$. For any open $H\subset Y_W$, the definitions give $(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X)(H)=\mathcal O_X(\Delta^{-1}H)=\mathcal O_W(\Delta_W^{-1}H)$. This identifies the restricted diagonal algebras, including their multiplication and units. No quasi-compactness of $W$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0E2X, lemma-existence-relative-dualizing, open-restriction observation; affine local finite presentation by Morphisms Tag 01TQ

proof.text: Pseudo-coherence restricts by restricting the local bounded-above finite-free representatives in [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Relative finite Tor amplitude also restricts: on an original amplitude neighbourhood, extend a test module on its intersection with $W$ by zero as a module over the restricted inverse-image base ring; the extension has the given stalks inside the open and zero stalks outside, hence restricts to that test module. Restriction of its derived tensor is the local derived tensor. Equivalently compute with a K-flat resolution; the amplitude vanishing restricts. Pullback and tensor restriction are [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde](1). Let $R$ be restriction to $W$ and $m_0$ the canonical comparisons of (1): on a K-flat resolution $P$ and any complex $N$ they are induced by the termwise equality $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N)|_W=\operatorname{Tot}(P|_W\otimes N|_W)$ and by $\mathcal O_X|_W=\mathcal O_W$, so they satisfy the associativity and unit laws (a strong monoidal structure on $R$) and carry the localization map $\mu_X$ [def-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-comparison] to $\mu_W$. Put $c=e_W^{-1}(\mu_{m_0};R(e_X(1)))$; it is an isomorphism by [lem-pc-open-restriction-evaluation-mate-is-iso] for this $m_0$. Naturality of $e_X,e_W$ [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] and of $\mu_{m_0}$ give $e_W(R\varphi;c)=\mu_{m_0};R(e_X\varphi)$ for every $\varphi$. With $D=\Delta_*\mathcal O_X$ the class map is $e_X^{-1}$ of $D\otimes^L D\xrightarrow{m}D\xrightarrow{\xi}Lp_1^*K$ by [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]; by step 1 the chain multiplication restricts to that of $D_W$, so $\mu_{m_0};R(m)=m_W$, and $R(\text{class map});c$ is the class map of $(K|_W,\xi_W)$. Hence it is an isomorphism. The same applies to $L,\eta$; for the scalar map use $\lambda_K$ and the unit law of $m_0$.

source.place: Tags 0E2T and 0E2X, definition-relative-dualizing-complex and restriction observation; cohomology.tex Tags 08DJ, 08DL

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-relative-dualizing-comparison] twice, to the supplied pairs $(K,\xi)$ and $(L,\eta)$ and the specified charts. All its assumptions are hypotheses of this item. It gives the flat finitely presented map $R\to A$, pseudo-coherent module objects $M_K,M_L$, their finite $R$-Tor intervals, and the actual diagonal classes $\gamma_K,\gamma_L$ with the displayed multiplication comparisons. The objects can be taken to be $R\Gamma(U,K|_U)$ and $R\Gamma(U,L|_U)$ because [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] specifies this quasi-inverse. In each Tor interval take the test module $N=R$: $M_T\otimes_R^L R\cong M_T$, so $M_T$ is bounded below (indeed bounded). By [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], $M_K$ has a bounded-above finite-free representative. These are exactly the two hypotheses needed for the affine internal-Hom comparison; no absolute perfectness of $M_K$ is being asserted.

For $T=K,L$, apply [lem-sc-affine-pseudo-coherent-rhom-qcoherent] with $P=M_K$ and second object $M_T$. Step 3 checks its bounded-above finite-projective source and bounded-below target hypotheses. It gives the requested isomorphism $\widetilde{R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_K,M_T)}\cong R\mathcal Hom_U(K|_U,T|_U)$ in the derived category, not just cohomology isomorphisms. The canonical normalization is the evaluation comparison: if $E$ is the bounded-above finite-free representative and $F$ a bounded-below representative of $M_T$, [lem-sc-derived-hom-finite-free-model] computes the sheaf side by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\widetilde E,\widetilde F)$. Choose bounds $E^p=0$ for $p>b$ and $F^q=0$ for $q<c$. In Hom degree $n$ a nonzero factor requires $c-n\le p\le b$, a finite interval. Thus its degree $n$ consists of only finitely many nonzero factors $\mathcal Hom(\widetilde E^p,\widetilde F^{p+n})$; each is the sheaf of $\operatorname{Hom}_A(E^p,F^{p+n})$. The componentwise map sends a homomorphism to its associated sheaf map and respects $d(h)=d_Fh-(-1)^n h d_E$. Hence it is the evaluation-normalized comparison and is natural in derived morphisms (the comparison before choosing these representatives is the transpose of the sheafified evaluation, using the tensor comparison [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde](3)).

source.place: Tag 0A6H, lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, (3)(a) and its proof; cohomology.tex lemma-Rhom-complex-of-direct-summands-finite-free

proof.text: The scalar morphism $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_K,M_K)$ is the transpose of $A\otimes_A^L M_K\to M_K$. By the tensor comparison and the evaluation normalization in step 4 its associated sheaf map is the transpose of $\mathcal O_U\otimes^L K|_U\to K|_U$. This is the scalar map of the restricted pair by [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]. By step 2 (the comparison $c$ built from $m_0$ via [lem-pc-open-restriction-evaluation-mate-is-iso] and the unit law of $m_0$) it is also the restriction of the scalar map on $X$. The internal-Hom object itself restricts by [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open]. This proves the assertion about the actual scalar map, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism of its target.

source.place: Tag 0E2V, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, scalar-map normalization; cohomology.tex Tag 08DL

proof.text: The equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] is fully faithful and triangulated, and its target is the full subcategory of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology. It therefore gives, for every integer $i$, the asserted Hom bijection by applying it to $(M_K,M_T[i])$. It preserves and reflects isomorphisms: an inverse is taken to an inverse; conversely full faithfulness lifts an inverse and its two identity equations. Thus $a$ and $\alpha_U$ correspond bijectively. On $\operatorname{Spec}B=U\times_VU=U\times_SU$, [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde](2) identifies the sheafification of $a\otimes^L_{A,p_1}B$ with $Lp_{1,U}^*\alpha_U$. The comparison for each supplied pair identifies $\gamma_K,\gamma_L$ with $\xi_U,\eta_U$ by [lem-trf-affine-relative-dualizing-comparison]. Applying the faithful affine functor over $B$ to the two sides of $(a\otimes^L B)\gamma_K=\gamma_L$ gives exactly $(Lp_{1,U}^*\alpha_U)\xi_U=\eta_U$. Faithfulness gives the converse.

source.place: Tag 0E2U and Tag 0E2W, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing, first paragraph; perfect.tex Tags 06Z0, 08DW

proof.text: Finally all comparisons use associated sheaf maps, tensor maps, evaluation and the units. On Hom complexes the identities $\widetilde{rh}=r\widetilde h$ and $\widetilde{g\circ h}=\widetilde g\circ\widetilde h$ prove scalar and composition compatibility. These componentwise identities descend to derived morphisms: associated sheaf is exact, so it sends the quasi-isomorphism in any roof to an isomorphism, and preserves composition with its inverse. Naturality of the evaluation transpose from step 4 then gives the same identities independently of representatives. Restricting further to an open simply restricts the same evaluation map, through the comparison $c$ of step 2 for the canonical $m_0$ [lem-pc-open-restriction-evaluation-mate-is-iso] and [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open]. On a smaller affine chart, pullback is scalar extension by [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde](2), so the same transpose describes the affine comparison there; the class comparison restricts as expressly asserted in [lem-trf-affine-relative-dualizing-comparison]. This proves compatibility also when a smaller chart is not a principal open. For $W=\varnothing$ the module category is the zero category, the diagonal algebra and both classes are zero, and every asserted pair condition is automatic. For an empty affine chart $A=0$, both derived categories are zero and the Hom and isomorphism correspondences are the unique bijections.
